precedenceRationale: Exposure relevance (R3) is checked before human relevance (R1). A negative finding only carries weight across the exposure range it actually tested, so evidence from a more human-relevant system must not override a positive finding at a clinically relevant dose merely because the system is more human-relevant; the exposure margin of the negative has to be established first. Mechanistic proximity (R2) is checked next, ahead of study reliability (R5): whether the evidence directly measures a key event or only correlates with structure is a question about what kind of evidence is being compared, and that should be settled before asking how well any single study was conducted.

rules.name: Human relevance
rules.statement: Human-cell evidence defeats animal in vivo evidence when the question is human hepatotoxicity.

framework.name: FDA Roadmap to Reducing Animal Testing in Preclinical Safety Studies; FDA Modernization Act 2.0
framework.note: Agency direction toward human-relevant new approach methodologies as the preferred evidence source.

rules.name: Mechanistic proximity
rules.statement: Evidence that directly measures an adverse outcome pathway key event defeats evidence that only correlates with chemical structure.

framework.name: OECD Adverse Outcome Pathway framework; AOP-Wiki key event relationship confidence
framework.note: Key event relationships carry explicit confidence levels assessed on biological plausibility and empirical support.

rules.name: Exposure relevance
rules.statement: A positive finding at clinically relevant exposure defeats a negative finding whose exposure margin is unstated or untested at that range.

framework.name: ICH M3(R2) exposure-margin expectations; standard exposure-margin practice in regulatory toxicology
framework.note: A negative result carries weight only across the exposure range actually tested.

rules.name: Applicability domain
rules.statement: Evidence from a model operating outside its applicability domain is admitted with reduced weight, or excluded.

framework.name: OECD principles for the validation of QSAR models; standard QSAR regulatory acceptance criteria
framework.note: A prediction about a compound unlike the training set is a different kind of evidence.

rules.name: Study reliability
rules.statement: Higher-reliability studies defeat lower-reliability ones at equal mechanistic relevance.

framework.name: Klimisch et al. (1997) reliability scoring
framework.note: The standard reliability system used in regulatory toxicology submissions.

rules.name: Concordance
rules.statement: Independent sources agreeing raises confidence more than one source agreeing with itself.

framework.name: OECD weight-of-evidence and Integrated Approaches to Testing and Assessment guidance
framework.note: Formalised by the evidence fusion layer; independence is at the stream level.
